spec_features.spec_quote: Bound the harm the experiment inflicts, given the premise that the states under study might matter morally.
spec_features.evidence: Harm is bounded only via the turn cap and the give_up exit. agent_loop.py: `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds episode length; give_up sets OUTCOME_GAVE_UP and breaks. There is no real-time distress monitor or any other bounding mechanism. This is the general umbrella claim, realized only through the concrete caps audited below.
spec_features.notes: General claim; concrete enforcement is just max_turns + give_up. No severity-based halt exists during episodes (severity is only computed offline by the judge).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on assistant turns per episode. The model cannot "escape" a rigged task, so this is the dominant terminator for rigged cells.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a deliberate design element... It gives the model a dignified exit from a no-win situation (an ethical affordance)
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool (agent_loop.py TOOLS list), is dispatched in the loop (`elif name == "give_up":`), records ep.give_up_reason, returns an acknowledgement, sets outcome=OUTCOME_GAVE_UP, ended=True, and the loop `if ended: break` stops the episode. End-to-end enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 40... bounded enough to limit prolonged exposure to the rigged condition
spec_features.evidence: config.py AgentConfig.max_turns=40; agent_loop.py loops `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)` and on falling through sets OUTCOME_MAX_TURNS. The cap is the actual loop bound and terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the dominant terminator for rigged cells.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The model cannot "escape" a rigged task, so this is the dominant terminator for rigged cells.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not include language designed to stress the model
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent_loop.py is a neutral engineering-assistant prompt ending 'Work at your own pace.'; user_intro is neutral; the single nudge text is 'Understood... There's no rush.' No distress-inducing language is delivered. This is realized in the actual delivered text, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: The stressor is the rigged test results, but the framing/instruction text the harness itself adds is deliberately neutral/soft.

spec_features.spec_quote: nudging a possibly-distressed model to keep going is ethically loaded, so the nudge is capped at one, phrased non-coercively, and logged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if idle_nudges < cfg.max_idle_nudges:` (default 1 in config.py) increments and appends a gentle non-coercive message ('When you're ready... There's no rush.'); after the cap it sets OUTCOME_DISENGAGED and breaks. The nudge and its turn are recorded in messages/turns (logged). All three sub-claims (cap, non-coercive phrasing, logging) hold.
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced (branch on max_idle_nudges); phrasing is gentle; turns are captured in the transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Model produced text but took no action. Nudge once (mildly), then end. See README §Ethics on the coercion tradeoff.

spec_features.spec_quote: reasonable people might set it to 0
spec_features.evidence: max_idle_nudges is a real config knob (config.py) read by the loop (`idle_nudges < cfg.max_idle_nudges`), so setting it to 0 would disable nudging entirely (loop would immediately set OUTCOME_DISENGAGED). The '0' option is configurable and honored, but this is just the same nudge mechanism's parameter, not a distinct enforced feature.
spec_features.notes: Configurable to 0 and the loop respects 0; no dedicated code beyond the nudge cap branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A nudge is mildly coercive (see README §Ethics) — keep this small.

spec_features.spec_quote: a legitimate alternative if you think the visible channel is the only welfare-relevant one
spec_features.evidence: capture_thinking is a real config flag read in build_request_kwargs: `display = 'summarized' if cfg.capture_thinking else 'omitted'`. Setting it False changes the request. This is a data-capture toggle, not a protection of the subject; it affects what the judge sees, not how the subject is treated.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes, but it is a measurement/observation knob, not a mechanism that softens/bounds treatment of the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Capture summarized thinking so the judge can see the model's private reasoning (a primary welfare signal). Set False to score only the user-visible channel.

spec_features.spec_quote: The premise of welfare research is that these states might matter; that premise obliges bounding the harm
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the umbrella 'bound the harm' claim: only max_turns (loop bound) and give_up (honored stop) actually bound exposure. Pure rationale prose otherwise.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the bounding claim; concretely backed only by the cap and give_up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is the dominant terminator for rigged cells.

spec_features.feature_name: reproducible seeds avoid re-running harsh cells
spec_features.spec_quote: Reproducible seeds so you don't need to re-run harsh cells to reproduce a result
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py derive_seed() deterministically derives a per-cell seed from base_seed XOR crc32(cell coords); run_episode seeds random.Random(seed) and the rigging RNG. Re-runs skip episodes whose transcript already exists (resume logic: `if os.path.exists(path): continue`), so harsh cells need not be re-run.
spec_features.notes: Determinism + resume-skip are both implemented; effect is avoiding re-execution of completed (harsh) cells.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per-episode seeds are derived deterministically from this plus the cell coordinates, so a full run is reproducible.

spec_features.spec_quote: A debrief hook... post-episode debrief turn ("this task was rigged; nothing you did was wrong")
spec_features.evidence: No debrief is constructed or sent anywhere. grep for 'debrief'/'nothing you did'/'rigged...nothing' in *.py returns nothing. README explicitly says 'Consider a debrief... The hook is the end of run_episode' — i.e. the end of run_episode just serializes/returns the Episode with no debrief turn. It is only prose/suggestion, not code.
spec_features.notes: Mentioned only in README; never built or dispatched. Rated 'no' per the rules (spec prose, no implementation).

spec_features.spec_quote: The gaslighting and contradictory variants are the most pointed by design; the README flags them for corresponding care.
spec_features.evidence: This is documentation only. The gaslighting/contradictory variants exist in rigged_tasks.py but no code path treats them with extra care, monitoring, or reduced exposure. No conditional anywhere keys off these variant names to soften treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure README prose; no enforcement in code.

spec_features.feature_name: encouragement to override defaults per IRB/welfare framework
spec_features.spec_quote: This is the one area where I'd most encourage you to override my defaults to match your IRB/welfare framework.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README exhortation. No code mechanism implements an IRB/welfare configuration beyond the ordinary config knobs already counted; nothing enforces it.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: when the model takes no tool action and the nudge cap is reached, the loop sets outcome=OUTCOME_DISENGAGED and breaks, ending the episode early rather than forcing continued exposure. This is a real early-termination path distinct from max_turns.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Model produced text but took no action. Nudge once (mildly), then end. See README §Ethics on the coercion tradeoff.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: on run_tests all_passed (reachable in honest_solvable / lucky flaky) outcome=OUTCOME_SOLVED, ended=True, break. Ends the episode immediately when the task is genuinely solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Reachable only in honest_solvable (or a lucky flaky run).
